title: Fade
description: A lane in Cinque Terre seen from the cobbles, looking straight up between painted houses into a summer sky, and the thirty years of sun that come after it. Drag forward and every wall ages by the light it actually receives: the top floors, open to the whole sky, bleach and chalk first, while the low storeys, which see only the slot of sky between the eaves, keep their colour longest. The pink and orange walls turned to the sun go to pale plaster within a generation; the coral wall across the lane faces north, sees only its slot of sky, and keeps its red.
intent: Reality pieces, technique 8 (Fade): manipulate a real photograph physically. One photograph is baked into an annual solar dose per pixel (MoGe-2 metric point map; world up recovered from the facades' vertical faces, the lane's orientation from the photo's own sun fitted on the walls' shading one paint colour at a time; 144 sun directions over a year at 44 N, each with a screen-space depth-march visibility test against the houses across the lane, clear-sky beam x the Ligurian coast's sunshine fraction, plus sky-view factor x diffuse, at 1/4 resolution on CPU; then the thin things that have hung there for decades, SAM masks of the open shutter leaves, lanterns, bracket and gelato sign plus black-hat lines for the drying lines, hooks and rods, stood off their walls and marched again at 1/2 resolution along each wall pixel's dose-weighted mean sun and over its sky, so each leaves a crisp tan line of unfaded paint), the sky graded live as if through a polariser on MoGe-2's sky mask (clear sky re-shot as a cyan-cobalt that deepens to the zenith at the frame's centre, cloud keeping its own light), the photo's own illumination (to recover albedo), and a SAM mask of the one bare stone wall. Live, albedo becomes optical density, split into carbon black and cyan / magenta / yellow pigment, each fading exponentially with dose (yellow and magenta about 4x faster than cyan), and the lime render chalks. On old painted signs 'only the blue remains': https://www.maru-sin.co.jp/en/news_sanpo/january-2023_01/ ; yellow and magenta process inks are the least lightfast: https://printing.org/content/2018/03/28/a-customer-has-complained-that-a-poster-is-fading-almost-immediately-with-exposure-to
sources: Photograph: 'Low angle view of colorful Mediterranean buildings surrounding a bright blue sky' by Victor Rosario (https://unsplash.com/@victor_rosario) on Unsplash, Unsplash License (https://unsplash.com/license). https://unsplash.com/photos/colorful-mediterranean-buildings-under-blue-sky-9rFrYPdisXU (file: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1787152171273-de25142325a1, 6192x4128, Sony ILCE-6700, Cinque Terre). Cropped to 4:3 (columns 200 to 5704), resampled to 2000x1500. Normals, metric depth and sky by MoGe-2 (tools/depth/normals.py); the stone wall's mask and the thin occluders' masks by SAM 2.1 (tools/depth/segment.py); maps baked by tools/depth/bakes/fade (prep.py, dose.py, mat.py) into plate.webp, light.webp and mat.webp.
